question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics become a supported core Doctor surface after the prerequisite ownership stack lands?
rationale: The implementation introduces a new persistent lifecycle capability defined by an open RFC; passing tests and an environment gate do not establish permanent core ownership, support, or upgrade policy.

options.title: Sponsor with safety gates
options.body: Accept the experiment-gated core direction only after the WAL-safe reader repair, real behavior proof, and prerequisite main-branch contract are complete.

options.title: Defer the stack
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged while maintainers evaluate the prerequisite ownership and later update-planning slices together.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the implementation stack if lifecycle ownership and reconciliation should remain outside the OpenClaw core Doctor surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor with safety gates
recommendation.body: Accept the experiment-gated core direction only after the WAL-safe reader repair, real behavior proof, and prerequisite main-branch contract are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and Doctor architecture history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the product and persistence contract decision.
